frames.caption: Each cell holds the chance of one training height and one noisy value together. A row adds noise to one height; a column, divided by its sum, is Bayes: the chance of each height behind one noisy value.
Each column is Bayes' theorem: prior times likelihood, divided by the total. The prior is each height's chance before seeing noise, and the likelihood is how well it explains the noisy value.
Average the training heights with those weights and you get the best guess x̂₀ of where the noisy value came from. At step 99 the weights are nearly even, so the guess is the mean from scene 1.
With xₜ and x₀ both known, two bells pin down the earlier value xₜ₋₁: one from xₜ, one from x₀. Their product is a single bell, so this step back is Gaussian.
Sampling has no x₀, so the step uses x̂₀ instead. The exact step back mixes ten bells, one per height; a single bell built on x̂₀ has the same mean and a little less spread.
Start from pure noise at step 99. Each step guesses x₀, moves part of the way toward the guess and adds a little fresh noise, and every chain ends on a height.
Run the same steps on four dog photos, starting from a pure-noise image. At step 99 the guess is the average of all four dogs, and it sharpens into one dog as t falls.
Asking for a dog, or here for a tall person, multiplies the density by the chance of that label at each x, then divides by the total. The result is a new density, p(x | tall), with area 1.
With the exact best guess the sampler can only return training heights, so the data is everything it knows. A smoother guess, such as a fitted bell, returns new heights in between.
Five assumptions carry the whole chain from heights to a dog. Each links to the frame where it does its work.
Swap a convnet for a transformer and the loss and the sampler stay the same. The network is a fixed function, and what its design adds is a preference for which functions are easy to learn.
Every box above is a concept and every arrow an operation that turns one into the next. Click any box to go to the frame that teaches it.
